newsitem.title: USA: Data Dimensions buoyed by analyst report.
newsitem.headline: Data Dimensions buoyed by analyst report.

text.p: Data Dimensions Inc shares extended their gains for a second day Tuesday, a rise company spokesman attributed to positive comments contained in a newly issued report from brokerage Cruttenden Roth.
In the report released Monday, analyst Neil Cooper rated the stock a strong buy.
Tuesday, the stock closed at 30-1/8, up 1-5/8 from Monday and up nearly 6 points, or 23 percent from Friday's close.
Cooper said he boosted his estimates for 1997 revenues and earnings to $57 million from $33 million and to $2 per share from $1, respectively.
For 1998, he said he expected earnings of $4 per share, up from $2 previously.
The analyst said the firm's new ARDES 2K Direct software marks a potent addition to its line of year 2000 products.
"We believe that ARDES 2K Direct is likely to be the best product available to help...organizations fix the year 2000 problem during the...critical window of opportunity," he said.

Data Dimensions produces software that solves a problem plauging many older computers which were not designed to process dates correctly after December 31, 1999, often because they use only the last two digits of of a year.
Ardes 2K Direct, expected to hit the streets in February, is a computer-based training tool for organizations wishing to resolve their year 2000 fixes in-house, Cooper said.
